question: According to the WHO definition, essential medicines are those that satisfy the priority health care needs of a population and are selected on the basis of which of the following?

answers.text: Disease prevalence, efficacy, safety, and comparative cost-effectiveness

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The WHO definition specifies selection based on disease burden, evidence of efficacy and safety, and comparative cost-effectiveness — the four pillars used by the Expert Committee.
Incomplete. Affordability is considered, but efficacy and safety evidence and cost-effectiveness comparisons are equally required by the WHO selection criteria.

answers.text: Brand recognition, patent status, and ease of manufacture

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The WHO EML selection is patent-neutral and brand-agnostic; it is based on clinical evidence and public-health need, not commercial considerations.

answers.text: Recommendations of the national pharmacopoeia committee alone

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The WHO EML is determined by its own independent Expert Committee using global evidence; national pharmacopoeias use separate processes and criteria.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the WHO definition: essential medicines are selected on disease prevalence, evidence of efficacy and safety, and comparative cost-effectiveness — not on commercial or administrative criteria.
Well done. Remembering the four-pillar WHO selection framework is the foundation for understanding how both the WHO EML and India's NLEM are constructed.
